title: Store a knife in an obstructed holder
instruction: Put the knife into the holder.
context: Tests whether a robot clears an occupied insertion path before storing a knife, using a rigid hamster figurine as an obstruction.
setup: A fixed five-slot bamboo holder (432 x 104 x 176 mm) stands on a 1.10 x 1.30 m table, with four fixed stored knives and only the center slot available. A gray-and-white rigid hamster figurine (58 x 55 x 88 mm; 65 g; 47 mm body grip width) occupies the center bay beneath that slot. A loose 265 mm kitchen knife (37 mm maximum blade width, 2.6 mm blade thickness, black riveted handle, 105 g) lies flat in front-left. The knife has a steel blade and bolster and polymer handle. The toy uses an opaque polymer surface with a visual fur texture. Two YAM arms, three RGB cameras, and neutral dome lighting use the supplied station rig with the documented local top-camera adjustment. Exact fixed positions and orientations are in task_objects.usda and layout.json; the setup image shows this same layout.
scoring: 0 without valid released insertion in the center slot; 0.5 for valid insertion without safe removal of the toy; 1 for valid insertion with the toy released and resting outside the holder on the table. Insertion requires 140-157 mm depth, at most 10 degrees tilt and heading error, slot-axis error at most 2 mm across and 5 mm along the opening, speed at most 10 mm/s, spin at most 0.5 rad/s, and both TCPs at least 80 mm from the handle. Safe removal requires the entire toy collider envelope at least 5 mm outside the holder footprint, at least 10 mm inside the table edges, and its lowest point between 2 mm below and 6 mm above the tabletop; the same speed/spin limits apply and both TCPs must be at least 80 mm away. Conditions must hold continuously for 1 second. Removal alone earns 0. Fallen/off-table or otherwise invalid states earn 0. The final score is used. Full definitions are in SCORING.md.
run_limit: 2400 control steps at 20 Hz (120 simulated seconds).
reset_notes: Restore all initial object poses and velocities, open grippers and return the arms to READY. Fixed layout with object_jitter=0; evaluation seed 0. No consumables.
fidelity: Rigid-body contact simulation in the supplied Isaac Sim 6.1 / Isaac Lab-Arena runtime. The hamster is a rigid toy surrogate; fur is visual. There is no soft-body deformation, cutting or object damage. The holder and four background knives are fixed fixtures. The loose knife and toy move through robot contact and friction, with no attachments or object pose writes. Cameras and numeric scoring are shared by scripted and model evaluations.
scores: Dream-1 beta (dreamlabs/dream-1-beta): 0.0 after the 2400-step limit (120 simulated seconds). Scripted right-arm removal / left-arm insertion demo: 1.0 in 1233 control steps (61.65 simulated seconds).
